Model the green plots as vertices of a graph, with an edge between two plots that share a side.  A walk that visits every plot exactly once and returns to the start without revisiting any plot is a Hamiltonian cycle on this graph (equivalently, an Eulerian circuit in the line graph).  Necessary for such a cycle is that every vertex have even degree.  Inspection of the adjacency counts shows many green plots of odd degree (e.g., degrees 1 or 3 appear repeatedly).  Because the graph contains vertices of odd degree, no closed trail that uses every vertex exactly once can exist.  Therefore Earl cannot accomplish the requested walk.
